unit.title: Travel Gone Wrong: Airport Dialogues
objectives: I can understand key information in airport dialogues about delays, curfews, lost baggage, and missed connections.
I can use useful airport words such as voucher, curfew, rebook, and free of charge.
I can ask an airline agent for help in simple English.
unit.source: Live 互動英語 2026年8月號 p.51

passages.title: Problems at the Airport
passages.transcript:
[1] Flight Delay
Passenger: Hi. The screen says my flight is delayed. Do you know why?
Agent: Yes. We found a technical problem with the plane, and safety comes first. Boarding will start at 6:30 p.m. Here is a meal voucher for the airport restaurants.
[2] Airport Curfew
Passenger: My delayed flight was just canceled! What happened?
Agent: I'm sorry. This airport has a curfew. No planes can take off or land at night. The next flight leaves tomorrow at 10:30 a.m.
Passenger: Will you give me a hotel room?
Agent: I'm afraid not. We are a low-cost airline, so hotels aren't included. But we can give you a travel voucher.
[3] Lost Baggage
Passenger: My suitcase never came out. Here is my baggage claim ticket.
Agent: Let me help you file a report. What does your bag look like?
Passenger: It's a medium-sized black suitcase with a red tag.
Agent: Thank you. Please write down your phone number and address. We'll track your bag and call you when we know more.
[4] Missed Connection
Passenger: My first flight was late, so I missed my connecting flight to Tokyo.
Agent: There's another flight at 9:00 tonight. I can rebook you on it.
Passenger: Do I have to pay extra?
Agent: No. The delay was the airline's fault, so the change is free of charge. Please go to gate 12.

questions.stem: Dialogue 1: Why is the flight delayed?

options.feedback: Weather is never mentioned. Listen for the word "problem".
The pilot isn't mentioned. What did they find with the plane?

options.text: Because there is a technical problem with the plane
Because the airport is closed at night
options.feedback: That is the reason in dialogue 2, not dialogue 1. Listen to dialogue 1 again.

questions.explanation: The agent says "We found a technical problem with the plane, and safety comes first." technical problem / technical issue = 機械（技術）故障.

hints.text: Listen to dialogue 1 again. Focus on the agent's first answer.
Listen at slow speed. Key word: technical.
"We found a ___ problem with the plane, and safety comes first."
Full transcript is shown. Answer: a technical problem with the plane.

questions.stem: Dialogue 2: Why can't the passenger leave tonight?

options.text: The airport has a curfew, so no planes can fly at night.
All the hotels near the airport are full.
options.feedback: Hotels come up later, but they are not why the flight can't leave. Listen for "curfew".
Tickets are not mentioned in dialogue 2. What rule does the airport have?

options.text: The plane needs to be cleaned.
options.feedback: Cleaning is not mentioned. Listen to the agent's first answer again.

questions.explanation: "This airport has a curfew. No planes can take off or land at night." curfew（宵禁）= a rule that stops something at night.

hints.text: Listen to dialogue 2 again. What rule does the airport have?
Listen slowly. Key words: curfew, take off, land, at night.
"This airport has a ___. No planes can take off or land at night."
Full transcript is shown. Answer: the airport has a night curfew.

questions.stem: Dialogue 3: What does the passenger give the agent so the bag can be found and sent to her?

options.text: Money to buy a new suitcase
options.feedback: Nobody pays money in dialogue 3. What information does the agent ask for?

options.text: Her passport and her hotel key
options.feedback: These are not mentioned. Listen for the two things the agent asks.
She doesn't show a photo; she tells the agent about the bag in words. What else does she write down?

options.text: A description of the bag and her phone number and address

questions.explanation: She describes the bag (a medium-sized black suitcase with a red tag) and writes down her phone number and address, so the airline can track the bag and contact her (D).

hints.text: Listen to dialogue 3 again. What two questions does the agent ask?
Listen slowly. Key words: What does your bag look like? / phone number and address.
"It's a medium-sized black suitcase with a red tag." ... "Please write down your ___ ___ and address."
Full transcript is shown. Answer: a description of the bag and her contact details.

questions.stem: Dialogue 4: Why doesn't the passenger have to pay for the new flight?

options.text: Because he has a travel voucher
options.feedback: The travel voucher is in dialogue 2. Listen for the word "fault" in dialogue 4.

options.text: Because the airline caused the delay
Because the new flight is not full
options.feedback: The agent never talks about empty seats. Why is the change free?

options.text: Because he is flying to Tokyo
options.feedback: Tokyo is where he is going, not the reason it's free. Listen to the agent's last answer.

questions.explanation: "The delay was the airline's fault, so the change is free of charge." If the airline caused the problem, the airline pays. free of charge = 免費.

hints.text: Listen to the end of dialogue 4. Whose fault was the delay?
Listen slowly. Key words: fault, free of charge.
"The delay was the ___ fault, so the change is free of charge."
Full transcript is shown. Answer: the airline caused the delay.

questions.stem: The ___ gave every passenger a meal voucher because the flight was three hours late.

options.feedback: Baggage means bags and suitcases. Bags can't give vouchers!
A curfew is a rule about night hours. Who would give passengers vouchers?

questions.explanation: airline = a company that flies planes and carries passengers（航空公司）. A low-cost airline / carrier = 廉價航空.

hints.text: Who gives vouchers to passengers when a flight is late?
words: gave every passenger a meal voucher

hints.text: You need a word for a company that flies planes.
"Curfew" is a rule, not a company. It can't give vouchers.
Answer: airline.

questions.stem: The delay was our fault, so changing your flight is free ___ charge.
questions.explanation: free of charge = 免費 (no money needed). charge (n.) = 費用.

hints.text: Look at the words around the blank: "free ___ charge".
This is a fixed phrase meaning 免費.
The missing word is a short preposition: o_.
Answer: free of charge.

questions.stem: The airport has a ___, so no planes can land between 11 p.m. and 6 a.m.

options.feedback: A voucher is a paper you can use instead of money. It can't stop planes from landing.
A tag is a label on your bag. Which word is a rule about night hours?

questions.explanation: curfew = a rule that stops an activity during certain hours, usually at night（宵禁）. Some airports have one to stop noise at night.

hints.text: Read the second part: no planes can land at night. What kind of rule is that?
words: no planes can land between 11 p.m. and 6 a.m.

hints.text: You need a word for a night-time rule（宵禁）.
A "tag" is a small label on a bag.
Answer: curfew. Try the similar question below.

options.text: I lost two baggages at the airport.
options.feedback: Baggage is uncountable, so it never takes -s. How can we count it?

options.text: I lost two pieces of baggage at the airport.
I lost two baggage at the airport.
options.feedback: We can't put a number right before an uncountable noun. Try "two pieces of ...".

questions.explanation: baggage and luggage are uncountable nouns（不可數）. We can't say two baggages. Use a piece of / two pieces of baggage, or count suitcases (two suitcases).

hints.text: Is "baggage" a countable or an uncountable noun?
Uncountable nouns have no -s and need a unit: a piece of ...
Option A adds -s to baggage, which is not possible.
Answer: B. I lost two pieces of baggage. (Or: I lost two suitcases.)

questions.stem: Passengers on Flight 202, please ___ to Gate 8 now. Boarding will begin soon.

options.feedback: Organize means to plan or arrange something. We need a verb meaning "go".
Charge means to ask for money. Passengers are being told where to go.

questions.explanation: proceed to + place = go to（前往）. It is a formal word used in airport announcements.

hints.text: Look at the words after the blank: "to Gate 8".
You need a formal verb meaning "go"（前往）.
"Charge" means to ask for money. It doesn't fit.
Answer: proceed. Please proceed to gate 12 = 請前往 12 號登機門.

variants.stem: Because of the ___, the night market had to close at 10 p.m. during the storm.
variants.explanation: curfew = a rule that stops activities at night.
